offspring of women with a history of breast cancer experience higher psychological distress and greater unmet needs than their counterparts with no parental history of breast cancer.

(1) Offspring of breast cancer patients have significantly higher rates of anxiety and depression than offspring of controls, (2) offspring of breast cancer patients report higher rates of unmet needs than offspring of controls.

there is no evidence that children of breast cancer mothers experience psychological distress or unmet needs, and that there is no association between the psychological distress and unmeets needs of children of breast cancer patients and their mothers' cancer status.

there is an association between the offspring of BC patients and their psychological distress and un met needs.

offspring of BC patients are not at increased risk of psychosocial morbidity, but that there may be an increased vulnerability to psychosocial morbity in those with an existing history of psychological distress.
